predecessors.name: Ulaid
predecessors.text: central Ulster round Armagh, taken from the Ulaid by the Three Collas (infobox: preceded by Ulaid); the fall of Emain Macha is dated 450 in a tradition on the Ulaid page

successors.name: Kingdom of Ireland
successors.text: 'Rossa Boy MacMahon agreed to surrender and regrant his lands to the English Crown'; the territory became County Monaghan

ledger.x: The Three Collas 'supposedly took much of central Ulster from the Ulaid'; the battle of Achadh Leithdheirg is dated 'around 331', the victors killed Fergus Foga and burned Emain Macha; the page calls this 'mostly fiction' and says the actual year and circumstances are unknown.

[Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Mirror of tir-eoghain's 1130 vassal_end, a bridge: the page gives no end to the vassalage, only that the kingdom 'was at its peak in the 12th century, under king Donnchad Ua Cerbaill' (king list 1130-1168/1169).
Page silent on a date and on who took them: after the Norman invasion only the Monaghan portion 'survived' as Oirghialla and the Ua Cerbaill line on the king list ends with Muirchertach (1189-1194).
'The Louth portion became known as Uriel after the Anglo-Norman invasion.'

certainty.note: The page names dioceses and counties, no frontier.
